_note: OPERATOR CONFIG for the on-chain memecoin quant layer. Every number here is a POLICY CHOICE, not a market fact, and every registry is EMPTY by default - an empty registry does NOT mean a wallet is clean. The addresses below are placeholders for the operator to fill in; the code reports the registries as empty until they are populated.
_authority_note: Each threshold now carries its AUTHORITY. Research in AUTHORITATIVE_TRADER_STANDARDS.md established that most of these numbers are NOT industry standards: no regulator, exchange, professional body or academic text publishes a win-rate threshold, a profit-factor band, a max-drawdown band, or a constant minimum trade count. They are kept because they are operable, and they are labelled so a reader is never told a vendor convention is a standard. What IS citable here is the NIST sample-size formula, the Wilson interval, the Sharpe definition, and the GIPS retention and fee-basis rules.

chains.note: The top 10 memecoin networks by measured DEX 24h volume (DefiLlama per-chain total24h). L1 and L2 TOKEN NETWORKS are kept separate: Base, Robinhood Chain and Arbitrum each have their own token economy even though they settle on Ethereum. `landscape` prints the full registry with the layer split and the per-source reachability matrix.

thresholds._min_trades_meaning: VALIDITY FLOOR for the normal approximation, NOT a quality standard. NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 7.2.4: the approximation is 'valid for large N, (N > 30)'. The research is explicit that 'N > 30' is a validity condition, not a claim that 30 trades makes a win rate meaningful. Below this floor a wallet has a SAMPLE, not a profile.

qualification_sample_size.formula: N >= [(z_{1-alpha} * sqrt(p0(1-p0)) + z_{1-beta} * sqrt(p1(1-p1))) / delta]^2, plus the Fleiss/Levin/Paik continuity correction N = N' + 1/delta
qualification_sample_size.note: This is the gate `traders` applies to qualify a wallet. It is 21x the old hard-coded floor of 30. NIST: 'taking the value of the proportion defective to be 0.5 leads to the largest possible sample size.' The sample size is a function of the CLAIM, not a constant.

thresholds._min_win_rate_authority: NONE - NOT STANDARDISED. No regulator, exchange, professional body or academic text publishes a win-rate threshold for trader quality. Win rate is only meaningful WITH its confidence interval, which is reported alongside it as a Wilson score interval (NIST 7.2.4.1).
thresholds._min_profit_factor_authority: NONE for the THRESHOLD - ANALYTICS-VENDOR-CONVENTION. The definition (gross profit / gross loss) is uncontested; the bands are not. No regulator, exchange, CFA Institute, GIPS or professional body publishes an interpretation band.
thresholds._max_single_trade_pnl_share_authority: NONE - analyst choice. An anti-lucky-hit / anti-survivorship guard, not a standard.
thresholds.note: A wallet must clear ALL criteria. The trade-count GATE is the computed NIST sample size, not the 30-trade validity floor.

consensus.note: Trigger a trade only when >=N profiled wallets act on the same token within the window. Counts DISTINCT wallets, only from the qualified pool, and the window is reported with every count.
consensus._authority: NONE - analyst choice. No authority publishes a consensus threshold for copy-trading entry.

registries.note: The DEPLOYER registry is DERIVED, not hand-maintained: `leapspace/deployers.py` finds each token's creator on-chain (EVM: binary-search for the first block with code, then scan for the creation tx; Solana: the mint's oldest-tx signer, cross-checked against RugCheck) and seeds the registry with the evidence. The CABAL, EXCHANGE and INSIDER registries remain hand-maintained and are EMPTY by default - the anti-insider filter can only exclude a wallet it has been told about. With those lists empty the filter reports 'unknown' for every funding source and NO wallet is excluded for insider reasons - which is the honest result, not a clean bill of health.
registries._authority: NONE for the EXCLUSION RULE. No regulator, exchange, professional body, standard-setter or analytics vendor publishes a rule for excluding deployer-funded, sniper or bundler wallets from a copy-trading universe. The COMPONENT definitions are published - GMGN's insider / sniper / 'first 70 buyers' labels (https://docs.gmgn.ai/index/insider-traders-snipers-first-70-buyers) and Nansen's first-funder METHOD (https://docs.nansen.ai/api/profiler/address-first-funder) - but the COMBINATION is a construction and is labelled as one.

friction.note: Slippage 100bps = 1.00% per side. failed_tx_rate 5% means 1 in 20 orders never fills (the gas is still burned). Latency 2s means the fill uses the price AT the shifted time, never the price seen when the decision was made.
friction._authority: NONE for the numbers - analyst choice. But the fee BASIS of any risk measure derived from them must be DISCLOSED: GIPS 2.B.7 'The firm should use gross-of-fees returns when calculating risk measures' and 4.C.42 require the basis to be stated. A Sharpe computed after modelled slippage, gas and MEV is a NET-OF-FEES Sharpe and is labelled as such wherever it appears.

kill_switch.note: CODE-ENFORCED. Once halted, trading stays halted across restarts until an explicit reset with an actor and a reason. No LLM prompt can clear it.
kill_switch._authority: NONE for max_drawdown_pct - analyst choice. CFA Institute lists maximum drawdown as an APPRAISAL RATIO and warns it 'must be used with care', but publishes NO numerical band. This 20% must never be described as an industry standard. The 15-minute window is also far shorter than GIPS's annual measurement basis.

rug.note: Injected rug events are SYNTHETIC by construction and every injection is logged with its before/after price so the output is auditable. This is a stress test, not a claim about history.
rug._authority: NONE - stress-test parameters, not market facts. Correctly framed.

copy_trade.note: Finite bankroll. When funds are locked in open positions the trade is recorded with skipped=true and a reason - never silently dropped.

pool.note: The trusted pool is re-evaluated periodically: a wallet that stops trading, turns unprofitable, or is revealed to be cabal-funded leaves the FORWARD cohort, with the reason and a timestamp logged. Its HISTORY IS RETAINED in the reported record - it is never silently dropped and never retroactively restated. GIPS 3.A.9: 'Terminated portfolios must be included in the historical performance of the composite up to the last full measurement period that each portfolio was under management.'
pool._authority: ACADEMIC-OR-PROFESSIONAL-GUILD for the retention rule - CFA Institute GIPS 3.A.9 (https://www.gipsstandards.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/2020_gips_standards_firms.pdf). NONE for stale_days and the staleness window - analyst choice. GIPS publishes NO re-evaluation cadence for a copy-trading wallet pool; its published cadence is the annual reporting period.
